title: Structure and roles of individuals
summary: Describes the roles of the people involved in a building project, from the client and site management team to designers, surveyors, contractors and cost roles.

sections.heading: Client and site management
paragraphs: The construction of a building is a complex process that requires many professionals to work together. The client is probably the most important person, as they are the reason the project is going ahead; the client may be an individual, company or organisation and employs contractors directly or indirectly.
The site manager oversees day-to-day operations, while the supervisor and contracts manager provide other levels of control.
bullets: Site manager: oversees operations day to day; ensures work is safe, on time, within budget and to the right quality; takes on staff, prepares the site, plans the work, installs temporary offices, oversees material deliveries

Site manager also carries out safety checks, liaises with architects, engineers, surveyors and planners, ensures compliance with building regulations and health and safety legislation, and is first point of contact for the public and sub-contractors
Supervisor: sometimes known as the general foreman; main contact for all trades on smaller projects; reports to the contracts manager on larger sites
Contracts manager: oversees projects from start to completion on time and within budget; first point of contact for the public, clients, site managers and sub-contractors

sections.heading: Safety officer
paragraphs: The safety officer is responsible for reducing the risk of accidents on site.
bullets: Develops, implements and enforces policies that reduce accident risk
Inspects sites for hazards and sets procedures to overcome them
Identifies broken equipment, defective tools and other hazards
Determines the PPE required
Makes sure workers know how to operate and use tools and equipment
Investigates all accidents and near-misses
Responds to employees' safety concerns
Coordinates registration and removal of hazardous waste

sections.heading: Design and checking roles
paragraphs: The architect designs the project and leads the management team. Other professionals check and support the design and construction.
bullets: Architect: designer and leader of the management team; converts client ideas into a building design and working drawings; liaises regularly with the client

Structural engineer: works closely with the architect; calculates loads, forces and variances from wind and rain, looking at structural safety; sometimes involved in insurance claims, repair work and alterations
Surveyor (building surveyor): positions the building on the land, ensures Building Regulations are followed, discusses and resolves problems, ensures the building process is carried out correctly
Clerk of works: the architect's representative on site; ensures the building follows the drawings; checks standard of work and quality of materials; can sign a variation order
Building services engineer: designs internal services (heating and ventilation, plumbing, electrical distribution, fire protection, lifts, escalators, acoustics)

sections.heading: Contractors, co-workers and the local authority
paragraphs: The building contractor enters into a contract with the client to carry out the work in accordance with the drawings, bill of quantities and specification. Co-workers are people in a similar role or at a similar level, such as other electrical engineers or other building contractors you coordinate with.
The local authority is responsible for the look and structural integrity of buildings in its area and for checking compliance with access and ease of use under the Equality Act.
bullets: Each contractor tenders for jobs and employs specialists within the trade to undertake key roles
Local authority planning officers look at planning proposals
Local authority building surveyors monitor construction from the bottom of the foundations up to the final fixing
Local authorities must be informed, and permission obtained, before roads or pavements are closed while services are brought into a new construction

sections.heading: Cost and purchasing roles
paragraphs: Several roles deal with costs and materials. Each group holds the one below them responsible for the work being done.
bullets: Quantity surveyor: suggests construction methods within the client's budget; calculates labour and materials; visits site to measure work done for interim payments and final accounts
Buyer: sources all materials by obtaining quotations from suppliers, with delivery times and quality assurance
Estimator: breaks down the bill of quantities into unit parts showing what each stage costs a contractor, then adds company overheads and profit margins

flashcards.back: Probably the most important person, as the reason the project goes ahead. An individual, company or organisation that employs contractors directly or indirectly.

flashcards.front: What is the site manager responsible for overseeing?
flashcards.back: Day-to-day operations, ensuring work is safe, on time, within budget and to the right quality standards.

flashcards.front: Who does the safety officer's accident investigation cover?
flashcards.back: The safety officer investigates all accidents and near-misses.

flashcards.front: What does the safety officer coordinate regarding waste?
flashcards.back: The registration and removal of hazardous waste.

flashcards.front: What does the structural engineer calculate?
flashcards.back: Loads, forces, and variances from wind and rain, looking at structural safety.

flashcards.front: Who is the supervisor also known as, and who do they report to?
flashcards.back: The general foreman. On larger sites they report to the contracts manager.

flashcards.front: What does the contracts manager do?
flashcards.back: Oversees projects from start to completion, ensuring work is on time and within budget, and is first point of contact for the public, clients, site managers and sub-contractors.
People you work with in a similar role or at a similar level, such as other electrical engineers or building contractors you coordinate with.
Designs the project, leads the management team, and converts the client's ideas into a building design and working drawings.

flashcards.front: What does the surveyor (building surveyor) do?
flashcards.back: Positions the building on the land and ensures Building Regulations are followed throughout the process.

flashcards.front: Who acts as the architect's representative on site?
flashcards.back: The clerk of works, who also checks quality of work and materials and can sign a variation order.

flashcards.front: What does the building services engineer design?
flashcards.back: Internal services such as heating and ventilation, plumbing, electrical distribution, fire protection, lifts, escalators and acoustics.

flashcards.front: What does the quantity surveyor do?
flashcards.back: Suggests methods within budget, calculates labour and materials, and measures work done to produce interim payments and final accounts.

flashcards.front: What does the estimator add to each cost stage?
flashcards.back: Company overheads and profit margins, after breaking the bill of quantities into unit parts.

quiz.q: Who acts as the architect's representative on site and can sign a variation order?
quiz.why: The clerk of works acts as the architect's representative on site and can sign a variation order.

quiz.q: Who sources materials by obtaining quotations from suppliers with delivery times and quality assurance?
quiz.why: The buyer sources all materials by obtaining quotations from suppliers.

quiz.q: Who breaks the bill of quantities into unit parts and adds overheads and profit margins?
quiz.why: The estimator does this to show what each stage costs the contractor.

quiz.q: Who is the designer of the project and the leader of the management team?
quiz.why: The architect is the designer and is considered the leader of the management team.

quiz.q: Which role investigates all accidents and near-misses?
quiz.why: The safety officer conducts investigations of all accidents and near-misses.

quiz.q: Which role calculates loads, forces, and variances from wind and rain?
quiz.why: The structural engineer calculates these while looking at structural safety.

quiz.q: Which role is also known as the general foreman?
quiz.why: The supervisor is sometimes known as the general foreman.

quiz.q: Which role designs internal services such as heating, ventilation, lifts and fire protection?
quiz.why: The building services engineer designs the internal services within the building.

quiz.q: Who visits site to measure work carried out to produce interim payments and final accounts?
quiz.why: The quantity surveyor measures work to produce interim payments and final accounts.

quiz.q: Who must be informed, and give permission, before roads or pavements are closed to bring services into a new building?
quiz.why: Local authorities must be informed and permission obtained before any such work can begin.

quiz.q: On larger sites, who does the supervisor report to?
quiz.why: On larger sites the supervisor reports to the contracts manager.

quiz.q: Which role positions the building on the land and ensures Building Regulations are followed?
quiz.why: The surveyor, sometimes known as the building surveyor, does this throughout the process.
